title: The Black Hole at Our Center
objective: After this level you can describe Sagittarius A* and how astronomers found it.
summary: At the Milky Way’s heart lies Sagittarius A*, about 4 million Suns. Stars orbiting it revealed it; the EHT imaged it in 2022.

cards.headline: Our galaxy has a monster at its center, and we watched stars orbit it.
Following the stars
cards.body: About 27,000 light-years away, at the center of the Milky Way, stars race around an invisible object. By tracking their orbits for decades, astronomers worked out its mass: about 4 million times the Sun’s, packed into a region far too small to be anything but a black hole. One star, S2, circles it about every 16 years.

cards.headline: A prize and a picture
cards.body: Reinhard Genzel and Andrea Ghez shared the 2020 Nobel Prize in Physics for this discovery. In 2022 the Event Horizon Telescope released an image of Sagittarius A* itself.
